prompt: Simplify: $(x^2)^4$. Write your answer as a power of $x$.
hint: The outside exponent tells you how many copies of the whole bracket are multiplied together.

hints.text: The outside exponent tells you how many copies of the whole bracket are multiplied together.
$(x^2)^4$ is four groups of $x^2$, and each group holds $2$ copies of $x$, so there are $2 \times 4$ copies.

explanation: A power raised to a power means repeated groups: $(x^2)^4$ is $4$ groups, each holding $2$ copies of $x$.
Count all the copies by multiplying the groups by the copies in each: $4 \times 2 = 8$.
So $(x^2)^4 = x^8$. This is the power rule: multiply the exponents.

alternativeExplanations.title: Add them up with the product rule
steps: Unroll it: (x²)⁴ = x² · x² · x² · x².
Multiplying powers adds exponents: 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 8, so x⁸.

alternativeExplanations.title: Egg-carton picture
steps: Picture 4 cartons, each holding 2 eggs. Every egg is one copy of x being multiplied.
Total eggs: 4 × 2 = 8, so the answer is x⁸.
